items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: they'd have to put a pillow under Willie Smith's foot so he didn't jar the microphone

ctx.x: But see in those days, everybody didn't just depend on the rhythm section. Every man played with a beat. I remember, in fact, when Jimmy Lunceford was here, when they

recorded, they'd have to put a pillow under Willie Smith's foot so he didn't jar the microphone because he was patting his foot so loud. And most of the bands in those days, when you went to a dance you could hear the feet on the dance floor. Everybody was beating in time, it was one of those things you could hear the patting of the feet right along with the music. And this made a lot of the momentum in the swing more predominant. See, because everybody played with a beat. Today nobody plays together with a beat.…

I remember many a fight between the bass player and the drummer about who was right and who was wrong. Well today, nobody plays together. Everybody has got his own little thing and I think that DISTURBS the rhythm or the beat. Because everything predominantly in those days was played for people to dance by.
